name: ROGII Wellbore Geology Prediction 3rd Place Solution: five candidate TVT trajectories (3-family HMM, particle filter, Last-PS NN, Delta NN, Adaptive 1D SDF) fused by a sequential SoftMax gate
venue_link: Kaggle competition writeup: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/3rd-place-solution ; local copy C:/Users/Aadinarayan R/Desktop/CSE/projects/Erudition/3rd.txt
code_availability: Inference notebook public: https://www.kaggle.com/code/tereka/rogii-exp417-gnll-five-groupkfold-submit?scriptVersionId=340176212 (a local copy is already in the repo: rogii_exp417_gnll_five_groupkfold_submit.py, 2,868 lines; its weights come from the Kaggle dataset 'rogii-exp384-hmmpf5p816-nn-softmax-artifacts'). Training code for the NNs and gates is not public [uncertain]. Our repo has re-implementations: kaggle2ndplace/anchor_hmm.py (HMM), anchor_sibling.py (sibling reference), anchor_pf.py (PF), anchor_ensemble.py (two-candidate SoftMax gate with the CE term).
evidence_level: Competition writeup with CV, public LB and private LB for every component (self-reported but backed by Kaggle's hidden-test scoring); inference code public.
extreme_summary: Generate physically plausible TVT candidates (HMM, PF), add NNs and a correlation model that make different errors, and let a small BiLSTM gate output per-row convex (SoftMax) weights over the five candidates, trained on MSE plus best-candidate CE. Fold-safe CV 5.29 ft, but private 5.84 ft (public 6.04). The largest private gains came from reference-GR design (sibling laterals, self-prefix) and prefix-based rate initialisation, not from the gate.
task_definition: Predict TVT for every hidden row after the prediction start (PS) of each horizontal well from the trajectory, lateral GR, the typewell (TVT, GR, Geology) and the known heel TVT prefix; row-level RMSE.
inputs: MD, X, Y, Z, lateral GR (plus missing flag), known TVT_input prefix, typewell GR/TVT. Also sibling-lateral GR from training wells sharing the same typewell (aggregated into 0.25 ft or 0.0625 ft TVT bins), a self-reference (TVT_input, GR) template from the target well's own prefix, and spatial-distance-weighted siblings in one branch.
target_parameterisation: Physics models: hidden state = TVT position (structural coordinate TVT + Z), formation rate d(TVT+Z)/dMD, GR bias, reference family. Last-PS NN: offset TVT - last_known_tvt. Delta NN: row-to-row delta TVT_t - TVT_(t-1), integrated from PS. SDF: a softmax over 256 typewell TVT candidates, expectation output. Gate: convex weights over the five candidate values.
output_representation: Five point-estimate trajectories (the PF also exports quantile, spread, skew and IQR features, and the Last-PS NN a Gaussian sigma), then a per-row softmax weight vector over K = 5 candidates, then a point estimate.
architecture: (1) 3-family HMM mixture: Exp417 base (weight 0.5; two typewell/sibling reference mixtures 0.2/0.8, self-prefix reference, bias state, exact forward-backward), Local-DTW HMM (0.2), fine-bin 0.0625 ft sibling HMM (0.3). Student-t (df=1) GR emission. The last 128 prefix rows are prepended with clamped TVT; initial rate comes from the last 256 prefix rows; output projected with a rate cap of 0.25 and at most 10 ft integrated correction. (2) PF: 500 particles x 240 seeds x 3 seed bases, rate momentum 0.9995, hard/soft observation families (f015), reference flag per particle, genealogy smoothing, likelihood-weighted seed averaging; candidate = 0.6 f015 + 0.4 soft. (3) Last-PS NN: 49 features into 96 channels; 16 dilated-TCN residual blocks (kernel 7, dilation 1..128 twice); MaxViT1D attention after blocks 4/8/12/16; downsampled typewell cross-attention after block 8 (residual encoder + gated BiLSTM); gated LSTM head; Gaussian mean/variance head. (4) Delta NN: same family, 31 difference features, dropout 0.5, manifold mixup. (5) Adaptive 1D SDF: TCN encoders for lateral and typewell, 128-d cosine correlation volume over 256 typewell TVT candidates fused with trajectory/rate/graph-edge cost, prefix-estimated GR bias/scale, softmax T = 1.75, expected TVT. (6) Gate: BiLSTM (hidden 32, 1 layer) or CNN (hidden 32, k = 7, 2 residual blocks) producing per-row logits over the 5 candidates. (7) 5 GroupKFold folds x 5 split patterns = 25 checkpoints per family; final = BiLSTM gate only (CNN weight 0).
core_mechanism: Propose-then-select under a convex constraint. Diverse candidates with different error structures (smooth global HMM path, multimodal PF, anchor-offset NN, local-slope delta NN, direct correlation SDF). The gate only reweights them per row using context: candidate disagreement, distance from PS, GR-missing flags and the NN's predictive sigma. The convex hull prevents extreme extrapolation with only 773 wells, at the cost of never correcting drift shared by all candidates. The deeper mechanism behind private generalisation was better reference GR and prefix use in the physics models.
training_objective: HMM/PF: none (probabilistic inference). Last-PS NN: Gaussian NLL with sigma^2 = softplus + 0.001; RMSE to GNLL improved 5.4176 to 5.3645 on the 3-split ensemble. Delta NN: delta RMSE (a GNLL pilot was worse). SDF: candidate CE + 0.25 SmoothL1(TVT/10) + 0.10 delta + 0.05 Rank-N-Contrast. Gate: MSE(y, sum w_k c_k) + CE(w, argmin_k |c_k - y|), 8 epochs.
decoding: Per-row convex combination sum_k softmax(logits)_k * candidate_k, averaged over 25 gate checkpoints. The HMM uses the forward-backward posterior mean; the PF uses the likelihood-weighted mean of smoothed paths; the SDF uses the softmax expectation; the NN uses the Gaussian mean.
metric_consistent_decode: Mostly RMSE-consistent. The MSE term and the convex mixing hedge between candidates, and the candidates are mean decodes. The CE-to-best-candidate term pushes toward hard selection (mode-seeking), which raised our pooled RMSE when we tried it (see gap).
evidence_scope: Whole lateral (bidirectional HMM/BiLSTM), against the typewell plus sibling laterals from other wells sharing the typewell, plus the target well's own prefix as a self-reference.
prefix_conditioning: Strong: the last 128 prefix rows are prepended inside the HMM with clamped TVT states; initial formation rate uses a robust estimate over the last 256 prefix rows (30 to 256 rows gave -0.042 private); a self-prefix GR template is mixed into the reference; the NN anchors on last_known_tvt; the SDF estimates GR bias/scale from the prefix.
propose_vs_select: Explicit propose (5 candidates) plus select (sequential SoftMax gate). An unconstrained BiLSTM refiner was worse (5.4023 vs 5.2797 CV, lost in 5/5 folds).
physical_constraints: TVT + Z structural coordinate with a slowly varying rate state (momentum), rate capped at 0.25 and integrated correction capped at 10 ft, slowly drifting GR bias, heavy-tailed emission, convex-hull constraint on the final output.
dataset: ROGII Kaggle: 773 training wells, 3,783,989 rows, with hidden test wells; 5-fold GroupKFold by well gives 155/155/155/154/154 validation wells (the same fold size as our 155-well holdout).
synthetic_to_real: No synthetic wells. Lateral-vs-typewell mismatch is handled by the GR bias state, sibling-lateral references (same tool and resolution as the lateral), self-prefix references and prefix-estimated GR bias/scale in the SDF.
metric_and_performance: RMSE ft (CV / public / private): 3-family HMM 5.970 / 6.207 / 6.229; PF 6.583 / 7.011 / 6.725; Last-PS NN 5.472 / 6.074 / 5.903; Delta NN 5.770 / 6.093 / 6.102; Adaptive 1D SDF 9.542 / 8.502 / 8.837; CNN gate 5.426 / 6.027 / 5.814; BiLSTM gate 5.333 / 6.043 / 5.836; final 5-split ensemble 5.288 / 6.043 / 5.836. The gate's gain over the best single candidate (Last-PS NN) is -0.14 CV but only -0.07 private. Private-LB interventions: spatial-distance-weighted sibling HMM 5.817 to 5.691 (-0.126); rational distance weighting -0.097; 30 to 256-row rate window -0.042; 3 to 5 split patterns 5.903 to 5.836 (-0.067); Rao-Blackwellized PF bias -0.003; fold-specific HMM reference pools -0.008.
comparability: Moderately comparable: same data and metric, and a CV fold size equal to our 155 holdout wells, but different well assignment. Their CV-to-private gap (about +0.5 ft for every component, including training-free HMM/PF) means our 4.84 ft holdout is best compared with their CV numbers (5.29), not private (5.84) [uncertain].
validation_protocol: Two-stage fold-safe OOF: base candidates for gate training come only from fold models that did not see the well; base models and gates share fold assignments; fold-local normalisation; 5 splits x 5 folds; no public-LB selection. The CV 5.29 vs private 5.84 gap (+0.55) is NOT mainly gate selection bias. Training-free components show similar gaps (HMM +0.26, PF +0.14), and the NN shows +0.43, so most of the gap is a test-set distribution shift. The gate itself realised about half of its CV gain on private (-0.07 of -0.14).
inference_budget: Heavy CPU physics (240-seed x 500-particle PF, 3 HMM families) plus 25 checkpoints each of 3 NN families and the gate, run inside Kaggle notebook limits; exact per-well time not reported [uncertain]. Physics features were recomputed on the hidden test set in-notebook.
repeated_layers: Handled indirectly by diversity: the PF keeps multimodal hypotheses (quantile/spread/skew features), the HMM keeps reference families as separate hidden states, and the gate can shift weight toward a different candidate where candidates disagree. Band confusion is only fixed if some candidate is on the right band, because a convex mix of two wrong-band candidates is still wrong or blended. The largest lever was reference quality (sibling laterals), which sharpens the likelihood and so reduces band ambiguity at the source.
drift: Explicit: rate state with momentum, a robust 256-row prefix rate estimate, prepended prefix with clamped TVT, and rate/total-correction caps. The Delta NN models local slope. They state the gate cannot fix drift shared by all candidates (an OOF oracle confirmed this ceiling) and name drift as the dominant private-test error for long hidden sections.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Gaussian predictive sigma from the Last-PS NN (GNLL) and PF spread/IQR are used as gate features, not as outputs. No reliability/ECE analysis. GNLL training improved the mean itself (acting as a learned loss attenuation).
where_to_use: (1) As a design template for a K-candidate gate whose candidates are hypotheses extracted from our own posterior (per-mode means of the ConvNeXt/FastViT per-column softmax), plus the expectation decode and physics candidates. (2) The physics-side levers (sibling references, self-prefix reference, 256-row prefix rate estimate, prefix prepended in the HMM) as new input channels or reference curves for our cost image. (3) The 5-split x 5-fold protocol as a lesson on selection: evaluate any learned gate with nested cross-fitting.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%) via diverse candidates and sibling references; drift (~25%) via the prefix rate state; the gate itself mainly targets blend/wrong-mode choice.
gap_vs_our_implementation: [uncertain: whether sibling-as-cost-image-channel was tried in the ConvNeXt path] Already tried in our repo: (a) a two-candidate SoftMax gate (ConvNeXt vs AnchorCNN) in kaggle2ndplace/anchor_ensemble.py, with and without the CE term: gate 5.017 / gate+CE 5.013 / bias-fixed gate 5.178 ft, versus one fitted global weight 4.870-4.905 and ConvNeXt alone 4.937 (row-wise oracle 4.011). The gate improves the median well (2.747 vs 2.835) but picks confidently and wrongly on catastrophic wells. This matches the 'learned per-point gates failed' entry in the context. (b) Sibling-lateral reference (anchor_sibling.py): 0.5 typewell + 0.5 sibling beats the typewell on 77% of wells; used in the PF (X_sibfull_w075: 12.08 vs 12.73 ft) and as an AnchorCNN channel stacked on PF channels (C_s1_pf_sib 6.09 ft, REJECT). (c) An HMM (anchor_hmm.py) was built but only tuned on subsets (~23 ft) and never scored on the holdout, versus their 5.97 ft. Not done: (1) no candidate set drawn from our own posterior; our gates mixed two models, not K modes of one calibrated posterior, and we have not built their 5-candidate diversity (HMM, Delta, SDF). (2) The sibling reference has never been fed to the ConvNeXt/FastViT cost image (the 16-channel image is built against the typewell only), and never alone in the CNN. (3) No self-prefix GR template as a reference channel. (4) No Gaussian-NLL / sigma head as a gate or calibration feature on the U-Net side (ours is a per-column softmax, which already carries uncertainty). (5) No multi-split cross-fitting of any learned combiner; our gates were fitted on about 124 wells in one 5-fold pass over the 155 holdout wells, versus their 773 OOF wells.
proposed_experiment: E1 (highest value, low GPU): sibling reference as a second cost-image source. In the 1st-place feature builder (kaggle_1st_place/solution/experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py and its cost-image code) add channels computed against the anchor_sibling.py profile (0.5 typewell + 0.5 sibling, 1 ft bins, the query well excluded, built only from training wells) alongside the typewell channels. Train FastViT-SA12 distilled for 150 epochs with the same seed; control = the current 4.84 ft student. Accept if the gain exceeds 0.39 ft or if the pair with the non-sibling model beats 4.69 ft. Synthetic wells need a proxy sibling (e.g. a perturbed copy of their own generating typewell) [uncertain]. E2 (no training): a posterior-mode candidate gate. From seq_NN_posterior_dump.py --save-all posteriors, extract K <= 3 per-row modes (peak finding, per-mode mass and mean) plus the expectation decode. First measure the oracle over these candidates, then fit a tiny cross-fitted convex gate (anchor_ensemble.py's Gate adapted to K inputs, features = mode masses, mode separation, distance from PS, GR missing) with MSE loss only (no CE, which is mode-seeking), nested 5 splits x 5 folds over the 155 wells. Compare against the expectation decode; per the context's metric fact this can only win if the gate adds evidence the posterior lacks (e.g. sibling or prefix GR-score features per mode), so include a per-mode sibling GR-consistency feature. E3: score anchor_hmm.py on the holdout with the 3rd-place settings (prepend 128 prefix rows, 256-row rate window, sibling 0.2/0.8 reference, Student-t df = 1); if under 7 ft, add it as a blend member and measure residual correlation versus FastViT.
implementation_effort: E1 medium (feature builder plus synthetic-well sibling proxy); E2 low-medium (mode extraction and adapting the existing gate); E3 low-medium (code exists, needs tuning and a full holdout run).
gpu_cost: E1: one 150-epoch FastViT run on the RTX 5060 8 GB (same as the baseline; 2-4 extra input channels add negligible memory), plus about the same again if the ConvNeXt teacher is retrained for KD. E2 and E3: CPU or a few GPU-minutes.
distillation_compatibility: E1: yes; sibling channels are inputs consumed by teacher and student, and KD on posteriors is unchanged (the teacher should also see the channels). E2: post-hoc on the student's posterior, so fully compatible. A multi-model candidate gate like theirs is not distillable into a single FastViT, but it can sit after it.
error_correlation_with_ours: Their candidates are highly diverse (HMM/PF are training-free physics; our PF residual correlation with the ConvNeXt is 0.20-0.33). Modes of our own posterior are, by construction, correlated with our expectation decode. Sibling-reference evidence is new information, which is the property the context says is needed.
risk: Our own two-candidate gate already lost to a single global weight (5.02-5.18 vs 4.87-4.91 ft), because about 124 fitting wells are too few for a per-row chooser and the gate is confidently wrong on catastrophic wells. Their gate had 773 OOF wells and still only realised -0.07 private versus -0.14 CV. Since our expectation decode is Bayes-optimal for a calibrated posterior, reweighting modes without new evidence cannot beat it. The 3rd place's final 5.84 private is worse than the 1st place approach we reproduce, so copying the whole stack is not a path to lower RMSE; the transferable parts are the reference-GR and prefix levers. Sibling references also carry a leakage risk if the query well or holdout wells enter the sibling bank (anchor_sibling.py guards the query well; the holdout wells must also be excluded).
notes: Warning about selection: the CV 5.29 to private 5.84 gap is common to all components (training-free HMM +0.26, PF +0.14), so it reflects a harder test set rather than gate overfitting, but the gate's marginal gain halved out of sample. Their own takeaway (paraphrased): prioritise the right reference GR, stable initial-rate estimation, diverse HMM error modes and well-level CV diversity before adding model complexity. Increasing the number of CV split patterns was itself a private-LB gain (-0.067). Related items: A05 (PF), 1st place writeup (1st.txt) for PF-heatmap channels, B06 (differentiable PF). The repo already contains the 3rd-place inference notebook (rogii_exp417_gnll_five_groupkfold_submit.py), which can be mined for exact HMM/PF hyperparameters.
